rules.guidance: Untrusted input concatenated into SQL, a shell command, or `eval`/dynamic code is an injection flaw. Use parameterized queries / safe APIs.
No hardcoded credentials, API keys, tokens, or private keys in source. Use config/secret stores.
User-controlled data written to HTML/DOM without escaping is XSS. Encode on output; avoid raw HTML sinks.
Don't use MD5/SHA1/DES/ECB for security; use a vetted algorithm (e.g. SHA-256+, AES-GCM) and a CSPRNG.
Server-side requests to a user-controlled URL/host risk SSRF; validate/allowlist the destination.
Deserializing untrusted data with a type-permissive deserializer enables RCE; constrain types or use a safe format.
Sensitive operations must check authorization (ownership/role), not just authentication — watch for missing checks on new endpoints.
Don't log secrets, tokens, full PII, or full request bodies; redact.
